proof_summary: Pell and companion Pell identities, together with their unimodular determinant, give a best-approximation bound for \(\sqrt2\); this controls fractional parts and yields a floor-shift identity, hence self-similarity of the summands on Pell-number blocks. Summing that identity gives \(b_{m+2}=(1+(-1)^m)b_{m+1}+b_m\) for \(b_m=a(P_m)\), from which induction yields \(b_{2t}=2t\) and \(b_{2t+1}=1\), providing arbitrarily large values.
